notes: Re-review after merging current main (9374e55) into this branch with zero conflicts, and after four further fixes described below. Bound to the freshly rendered bytes at masterSha256 e4bb99bd...2e301e, produced by offlineGeneratedPlanRender.ts rendering the same real generated six-beat production plan for compare-rtx4080s-rtx4080. All seven frames re-extracted from THESE bytes and individually inspected.

FIX 1 — THE GENERATED PLAN NOW CONTROLS THE SHOT LIST. deriveUiRenderState was called once per plan and every non-hook beat reused the result, so five beats asking five different questions resolved to five requests for one identical screenshot. Previous rounds recorded that as an honest limitation; it is really the plan failing to control the render. The verified STATE is still derived once (same parts, same resolution, same preset, so no beat can show different numbers), but the FRAMING now comes from each beat's own purpose: commitment frames the matchup cards, evidence the per-game FPS table, reversal the value-per-frame row, payoff the verdict tally, cta the share control. Every anchor is text Compare already renders, and capture.ts's focusOn fails loudly if one is missing. framing is part of stateIdentifier, so the same-state determinism guard treats two framings as two legitimate captures rather than as a violation, and an unrecognised framing throws instead of silently rendering the default crop. Result in these bytes: five DISTINCT UI captures (md5s all different) where every previous round had one or two.

FIX 2 — AN UNQUALIFIED PRICE THAT ONLY BECAME VISIBLE ONCE THE CROPS MOVED. The new cta framing put Compare's part row on screen, which rendered 'Ryzen 9 9950X3D  $669' with no qualifier. That figure is cpus.json's price_usd — SpecSmith's own editorial estimate — presented as if it were a price someone charges. PartSelector's selected-part price, PartCard's list price, and PartCard's aria-label (so a screen reader heard the unqualified version too) all rendered it bare. All three now read 'Est. $669' / 'estimated $669'. Verified in beat6 and the closing frame of THIS render: the row reads 'Est. $669'. A part with no catalogue price still says 'Price at retailer' rather than inventing a number.

FIX 3 — MONETARY PROVENANCE IS NOW ENFORCED, NOT REVIEWED BY EYE. qualityReviewer.ts gained a closed PriceProvenance set (verified-retailer-observation, source-reported-msrp, internal-editorial-estimate, test-fixture, unknown) plus priceSource/priceObservedAt, and checkPriceClaim fails closed on: no provenance, an unrecognised one, provenance 'unknown', an editorial price with no estimate qualifier, an MSRP with no MSRP qualifier, a fixture value not identified as a fixture, a retailer observation naming no merchant or no observation time, and live-retailer wording (real/live/current/actual/today/retailer) on anything that is not a verified observation. The wording rule reads the display label only: an earlier draft also scanned claim prose and flagged THIS file's own sentence 'not live or verified current retailer prices', punishing an accurate disclaimer. The price claim below is tagged internal-editorial-estimate, which is what price_usd actually is.

FIX 4 — CAPTIONS ARE DRAWN AS AN OVERLAY. Now that beats frame real tables and charts, white outlined text printed onto a table of numbers read as though it were part of the table. Captions use a padded, mostly-opaque backing band (ASS BorderStyle 3) instead of outline-only text, so they are unmistakably an overlay, legible at phone size against both the light bars and the dark page, and not dependent on colour alone. MarginV keeps the band below the region focusOn frames (the anchor lands near 34% of frame height), so each beat's primary evidence sits above the caption rather than behind it.

0.2s (beat 1, hook, video-generation capability): localFixtureVideo.ts's offline card. It no longer opens the video with a 68px 'OFFLINE FIXTURE' warning above a line of apology — that was a developer notice occupying the first seconds of every render. A small marker, 'OFFLINE FIXTURE - no paid provider called', is baked into the pixels at top-left inside the safe area, and the centre of the frame is left to the storyboard's own hook caption, 'Pick the GPU before / SpecSmith reveals the names…', fully inside the frame on its backing band. Honesty is unchanged and better placed: the marker survives metadata stripping, the background is deliberately not SpecSmith's palette, and isFixture / presentedAsRealSpecSmithUi still drive the gates. Verified in this frame.

3.5s (beat 2, commitment, framing=matchup): real /compare, RTX 4080 Super vs RTX 4080, r9-9950x3d both sides. 'Est. GPU+CPU: $2,128' / '$1,691', 'Est. Avg FPS: 164' / '160', 'Est. $13/avg FPS' / 'Est. $11/avg FPS' — every dollar figure explicitly qualified. 20-0 tally, 'Better Value' badge, per-game bars fully drawn with their value labels. Caption 'LOCK YOUR PICK' inside the frame on its band. No consent banner.

8.0s (beat 3, evidence, framing=chart): a GENUINELY DIFFERENT SHOT — the per-game FPS table with real paired numbers (Cyberpunk 101/97, MSFS 60/58, RDR2 113/109, Fortnite 167/163, Valorant 347/340, CS2 345/338) and a Winner column, plus the tail of the bar chart and its axis above it. Caption 'REAL SPECS • EST. PRICES • REAL RULES' on two lines, inside the frame; it overlaps the Apex Legends row, which is secondary content — the anchored primary evidence (the table header and first six rows) is above it.
14.5s (beat 4, reversal, framing=value): the $/avg FPS explanation line and both cards' Est. value figures, with the bar chart below. Caption "BUT HERE'S THE CATCH" inside the frame.
19.5s (beat 5, payoff, framing=verdict): the 20-0 verdict tally with both build cards and their Est. figures. Caption 'SPECSMITH RESULT' inside the frame.
23.0s (beat 6, cta, framing=cta): the share control and the part row now reading 'Est. $669'. Caption 'CONTINUE IN SPECSMITH →' / '/compare' — the exact CTA route — on two lines, inside the frame.
25.0s (closing, past the last caption cue's end at 24.0s): clean Compare state, no caption, no consent banner, 'Est. $669' still correctly qualified.

REMAINING VISUAL LIMITATION, MEASURED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. Five distinct captures by bytes is not five distinct compositions by eye. The matchup, value, verdict and cta regions sit within about one screen of each other on Compare, so at a 540x960 CSS viewport their crops overlap substantially: beats 2, 4, 5, 6 and the closing frame all show the 20-0 tally and the two build cards at slightly different scroll offsets. Counting what a viewer would actually perceive, this video has roughly three distinct compositions — the fixture hook card, the per-game FPS table, and the cards/tally area at four offsets — not six. That is a real improvement on every previous round, where five of six beats were one identical screenshot, but it is not the six-shot story the storyboard describes, and visualCoherenceScore/pacingScore below are deliberately left at 8 rather than raised. Genuinely distinct shots for those four beats would need either more separated regions than Compare offers or a second surface, which is beyond this PR.

No fake or generated UI is presented as real: the one non-UI beat is a plainly labeled offline fixture card. No fabricated benchmark or price data — every number in the real-UI beats is the app's own estimateFpsForBuild()/gpus.json/cpus.json output, and every dollar figure now carries an explicit Est. qualifier, including the part row that did not before.

AUDIO — SIGNAL ANALYSIS ONLY, NOT A LISTEN. This environment has no audio playback capability and nothing in it can hear the file, so audioReviewMethod stays 'signal-analysis-only' and the gate correctly refuses a passing audio verdict regardless of audioClarityScore. Measured on THESE exact bytes: AAC-LC 22050 Hz mono, 106 kb/s, audio duration 25.338005s against a 25.333333s h264 1080x1920 30fps video stream (audio 4.7ms longer, so nothing is cut short). silencedetect at -35dB/0.3s: ZERO intervals. At finer resolution (-45dB/0.05s) the only gaps are 0.07-0.21s inter-phrase breaks, the first at 2.10-2.30s which lands on the beat 1 to beat 2 boundary at 2.0s, so narration tracks the generated beat timeline. volumedetect mean -21.7 dB, max -2.0 dB. ebur128 integrated -21.5 LUFS, LRA 1.3 LU, true peak -2.0 dBFS. astats peak level -1.97 dBFS, flat factor 0.000000, one sample at peak — no clipping. First 0.5s mean -21.4 dB and last 0.5s mean -24.0 dB, so there is no truncation at either end. Two things a listener should still judge: -21.5 LUFS is roughly 7 LU quieter than the ~-14 LUFS short-form platforms normalise toward, and a 1.3 LU range is extremely flat — both consistent with synthetic espeak-ng narration rather than a human read. A genuine full listen is still required before audioReviewMethod can become 'listened-full'.

REPRODUCIBILITY. Same environment, same commit: THREE consecutive full renders produced the byte-identical master e4bb99bd...2e301e, each with five distinct UI captures at the same md5s. Cross-machine: NOT established, and the previous round proved it fails — a CI runner rendered ddccc97e... at 731,924 bytes against that round's local 726,691, a size difference rather than only container timestamps, most likely a different font stack and Chromium build. An earlier round's note attributing run-to-run variation to ffmpeg was at least partly a misdiagnosis of the racing UI capture fixed previously; within one machine the pipeline is now byte-stable. The evidence gate stays bound to this one sha256 and is expected to report NO MATCH on any other machine, which is the gate working.

claims.text: RTX 4080 Super and RTX 4080 Avg FPS values shown are SpecSmith's estimated FPS, not measured benchmark FPS.

The GPU+CPU prices shown ($2,128 / $1,691) and the derived $/avg FPS figures are SpecSmith's own static catalog price_usd values, explicitly labeled 'Est.' on screen — not live or verified current retailer prices.
The real Compare page state (both cards, prices, Est. Avg FPS, per-game bars) is shown live across the commitment, evidence, reversal, payoff, and CTA beats.
